# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 exporting manufacturers). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| supplier_diversity | Number of distinct input suppliers (standardized), 2021-2022 |
| export_growth_2023 | Export value growth in 2023 (percent index) |
| log_sales_2020 | Log sales, 2020 |
| years_exporting_2020 | Years since first export, standardized, 2020 |
| export_growth_2020 | Export value growth in 2020, standardized |
| buyer_rating_2023 | Average rating from foreign buyers, 2023 |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| product_group | Sector: durables / nondurables |
| inventory_days_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_imported_inputs_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| port_distance_km | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| certified_iso | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| debt_ratio_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of supplier diversification on export growth?

Approach: OLS of export_growth_2023 on supplier_diversity with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size, firm age, the pre-period value of the outcome and buyer_rating_2023, which captures an important determinant of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on supplier_diversity is -1.957 (SE 0.225, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: negative effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

analysis.py

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
y = df["export_growth_2023"]
lo, hi = y.quantile([0.01, 0.99])
df = df[(y >= lo) & (y <= hi)]
X = sm.add_constant(df[['supplier_diversity', 'log_sales_2020', 'years_exporting_2020', 'export_growth_2020', 'buyer_rating_2023']].astype(float))
fit = sm.OLS(df["export_growth_2023"].values, X.values).fit(cov_type="HC1")
print("n =", len(df))
print("coef =", fit.params[1], "se =", fit.bse[1], "p =", fit.pvalues[1])

content.text: Adjusting for buyer_rating_2023, a post-treatment variable, flips the sign from about +0.69 to −2.1.

input.content: {"decision":"reject","reason":"The reported negative effect (-1.96) comes from controlling for buyer_rating_2023, a 2023 post-treatment variable that supplier diversity strongly predicts (a mediator/collider). Without it, and with only pre-period controls, the coefficient is positive (about +0.69, SE 0.24, and similar with all pre-period controls), so the sign flips and the conclusion is not supported."}

content.text:
I rejected the report. Its negative effect of supplier diversification on export growth comes from one questionable control, and the sign reverses without it.

The analyst controlled for `buyer_rating_2023`, which is measured in 2023, after the supplier diversity measure (2021–2022). Supplier diversity predicts it strongly: a regression of the rating on diversity gives a coefficient of 0.66 (SE 0.03). Adjusting for it blocks part of the effect or introduces bias, so the −1.96 estimate isn't a clean effect of diversification.

I re-ran the specifications on the full sample of 2,000 firms. I did not reproduce the analyst's own run (1% trim, N = 1,960). I did not run `analysis.py` directly, but I fit the same model with the rating included, which is the source of the difference. All use robust (HC1) standard errors:

| Specification | Coefficient on supplier diversity | SE |
|---|---|---|
| No controls | +2.55 | 0.25 |
| Pre-period controls (size, years exporting, 2020 export growth) | +0.69 | 0.24 |
| All pre-period controls (adds region, sector, listing and the 2020 firm characteristics) | +0.69 | 0.24 |
| Pre-period controls plus `buyer_rating_2023` | −2.12 | 0.23 |

The report also states that it estimated only one specification, so it doesn't show the sign depends on that choice.

I wrote the decision and reason to `verdict.json` in the work folder.
